set.n: The 'Fontaine' murder cash, Mentor (no cache; wrong man named)
set.st: Treasure lists say wealthy farmer Thomas Fontaine, known to carry large sums, was murdered near Mentor in October 1904 and little money was found on him. The record says otherwise: the Grand Forks Herald of 21 Oct 1904 ('Fontaine Is Not Killed') found Phileas Fontaine alive, working at a meat market in East Grand Forks. The man murdered near Mentor about 17 Oct 1904, by his travelling companion, later held at Woonsocket, R.I., was Joseph Mongeon, a thresher and spruce-gum picker with a little threshing money. The treasure-list version names the wrong man; nothing was hidden.
set.tovw: Lead grade F (treasure thread): wrong man named; no wealthy farmer and no cache

src: Grand Forks Herald, 21 Oct 1904, p. 5, 'Fontaine Is Not Killed' (Newspapers.com 1134316227)
